podcast.title: Decca Executive's Disbelief in Holly (1956)
podcast.body: Paul Cohen, the executive at Decca who signed Buddy Holly, became thoroughly disillusioned with Holly's lack of success in 1956, reportedly telling friends that Holly was "the biggest no-talent I have ever worked with." "Paul Cohen, the executive at Decker who had signed Holly, at one point was telling his friends, Buddy Holly is the biggest no-talent I have ever worked with."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-One: "That'll Be the Day", by the Crickets

podcast.title: Authority Over Milt Gabler (1957)
podcast.body: Cohen informed Buddy Holly that Milt Gabler, despite being a vice president, reported to Cohen, clarifying that Gabler had no authority to override contractual agreements. "But Cohen explained to him that Gabler was only a vice president, and that he worked for Cohen."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode Sixty-One: "That'll Be the Day", by the Crickets

podcast.title: Refuses to Waive Contract Clause (1957)
podcast.body: Cohen refused Buddy Holly's request to waive a clause in his Decca contract that prohibited re-recording 1956 material for five years, indicating his firm stance on the contractual obligations. "Buddy tried to get Paul Cohen to wave that clause in the contract, when Cohen said no."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
